intro.title: Multiple State Variables
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive user profile form that manages multiple pieces of information simultaneously, such as a user's name, email, and age. You'll learn how to use multiple useState hooks in a single React component to track different state variables independently. This approach allows each piece of data to be updated separately while maintaining the component's overall state. You'll practice creating separate state variables, updating them with individual setter functions, and displaying the current values in your JSX. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to organize and manage complex component state using multiple useState declarations instead of cramming everything into a single state object.
intro.usecase: Multiple state variables are essential in complex React applications where different UI elements need independent state management. In e-commerce sites, you might track separate state for shopping cart items, user authentication status, search filters, and modal visibility all within the same component. Social media dashboards often manage multiple states simultaneously - like post data, user preferences, notification counts, and loading states for different sections. Forms frequently require tracking individual field values, validation errors, and submission status as separate state variables to provide responsive user feedback.
